subject: Testing independence of frequency of VP ellipsis between interlocutors

messages.author: 9d935d54c0e7b158
messages.subject: Testing independence of frequency of VP ellipsis between interlocutors
parts:
Hello,

I realize this is a very basic question, but I have been doing quite a
bit of reading and am still uncertain how best to proceed here. I do
have this book, so if I have overlooked something useful therein,
please feel free to refer me back to it. :)

My data consists of counts of a VP ellipsis used in conversations
between pairs of interlocutors (from the Switchboard corpus). The
hypothesis I want to test is the following: more frequent use of this
VP ellipsis by one speaker will tend to increase the frequency of the
VP ellipsis by the other speaker (i.e., this might be evidence of a
priming effect).

So I just have two vectors, the counts for speaker A and the counts
for speaker B are the columns, and if they are lined up each row
represents a particular conversation, like this:

A B
0 1
0 2
1 0
3 1
0 2
2 0
2 1

There are about 420 conversations (rows). There are lots of zeros in
this data. So the first row {0,1} means that in the first
conversation, speaker A used no VP ellipsis and speaker B used it
once.

What would be the best way to analyze this data?

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Testing independence of frequency of VP ellipsis between interlocutors
parts:
Gathering from your description that the data are dependent samples, I
think you will need a t-test or a Wilcoxon test for dependent samples,
both of which are not explained in that book (but in my stats book:
Sections 4.3.2.2. and 4.3.2.4 of
<http://www.amazon.com/dp/3110205653>).

Cheers,
STG

Thanks,
Alan
